newsitem.title: INDIA: India budget to be carried live on TV, Internet.
newsitem.headline: India budget to be carried live on TV, Internet.

text.p: India's federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on Friday will be broadcast live on state television and on the Internet.
Finance Minister P.Chidambaram is scheduled to unveil his budget proposals in a speech at 5.00 p.m. (1130 GMT) on Friday.

The speech will be broadcast live by state-run Doordarshan television, which would subsequently carry interviews and analyses in a six-hour live show, a spokesman for TV Today, which will produce the programme, told Reuters.
Chidambaram and senior Finance Ministry officials will be interviewed on the programme, which would include the speech and be interrupted only by Doordarshan's regular news bulletins, he said.
The programme is scheduled to start at 4.30 p.m., one hour before the speech, and will be in Hindi and English, he said.

The spokesman said Reserve Bank of India's governor Chakravarti Rangarajan would also be interviewed in Bombay during the programme which would feature opinions from stock brokers, economists, businessmen and common people.
TV Today will also have an Internet website (http://budget.allindia.com) which will carry the minister's speech soon after it ends, he said.
Citibank N.A. said in a statement its own website on the Internet would feature regular updates on the budget from 5.00 p.m. (1130 GMT).
There will be an online chat show at the site (http://www.citicorp.com/India) from 9 p.m. (1530 GMT), featuring industry leaders and former finance minister Pranab Mukherjee, it said.

The Indian Economy Overiew, a web magazine, said in a statement that its site (http://www.m-web.com) will publish pre-budget analysis and the full text of budget statements and reactions, and also host live discussions.
The coverage would include sound and video coverage, it said. It gave no details.
